timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Why is standing permission such a big problem?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: If an attacker compromises an account with permanent admin rights, they own everything. No barriers.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So JIT just turns on permissions when you need them?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. You activate, do your work, and the access automatically expires. Time-boxed elevation.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: And JEA is different from JIT?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: JIT controls WHEN you get access. JEA controls WHAT you can do with it. Even elevated users get limited.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So even with admin access I can't run everything?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Right. Role capabilities define exactly which cmdlets are allowed. No surprise commands.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What's a PAW? Sounds like a dog toy.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Privileged Access Workstation. A hardened, dedicated machine for admin tasks. No email, no browsing.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Do I really need a separate computer just for admin work?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: For high-security environments, absolutely. It's the cleanest way to protect sensitive operations.
